newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan leader tells war rally he will fight.
newsitem.headline: Sudan leader tells war rally he will fight.

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir told a boisterous war rally on Wednesday his country was ready to defend its borders against alleged attacks by Ethiopia and Eritrea.
Outside Khartoum's Friendship Hall, a convoy of more than a dozen trucks carrying food supplies -- with soldiers seated on top -- trundled by in a display of war preparations.

"We are on the path of truth," Bashir told the Sudanese Universities Union, implying that Sudan's neighbours were acting in concert with rebels in the east and south, supported by other countries he did not name.

"The Ethiopians started this war and the Eritrean government tells everybody it will open its land to whoever wants to bring down the government," Bashir said in a speech punctuated by shouts from the audience of "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest).

Sudanese rebels -- who deny any outside assistance -- are advancing on Damazin, about 480 km (300 miles) southeast of the capital. The town's hydroelectricity plant supplies Khartoum with 80 percent of its power.
Travellers returning from the area said on Wednesday Sudan was increasing its military and air presence in the strategic town.

It was standing room only in the building beside the Nile on the outskirts of Khartoum and the audience rose to its feet when Bashir, dressed in camouflage fatigues and waving a stick over his head, entered the room.

He said Sudan would stand up to enemies in the U.N. Security Council, which is due in February to impose an air embargo on Sudan for failing to hand over three gunmen charged with trying to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Addis Ababa in 1995. Sudan says the men are not within its borders.

"Those countries who control the United Nations and Security Council are using it to bring down the government," Bashir said. "It is part of the foreign plot in the region to undermine the Arab world."
Men in robes waving axes and sticks broke into an impromptu dance to a Sudanese war song played by violins and accordions as Bashir left the hall.
"Kheibar, Kheibar," shouted a woman. "Americans...and Jews, Mohammed's army is returning." Others in the audience took up the chant about a victory by Islam's Prophet Mohammed over a Jewish tribe.

"This is for God, not for power," another woman shouted from her seat when an official said Sudan had earmarked funds for war expenses. Sudan has tried to rally support for fighting the rebels with a call of jihad, or holy war.
Officials told the rally Sudan had foreign backing. They said Jordan's King Hussein has expressed support and newspapers reported Qatar had sent two planes of supplies.

Outside, the president watched more than a dozen trucks file slowly past loaded with burlap sacks of dates and other food. Soldiers wearing red headbands rode atop pumping their fists in the air and chanting.
"One million martyrs to sacrifice for unity," said banners draped across the Peoples' Defence Force trucks. A woman cheering the convoy said: "Look how many there are."
"You have seen the convoys from the northern state loaded with food, money and mujahideen (holy fighters)," Bashir told reporters on the steps of the hall.
"We hope to have positive results to unite Sudan," the Sudanese president said before being driven away in a champagne-coloured Mercedes car.
